theses.headline: West African copperbelt-adjacent and central-African copper producers outperform over 12 months as copper's 12-month price surge (+36.8%) compounds with DRC/Zambia project financing momentum.
theses.rationale: Copper is the strongest-momentum industrial metal in the commodity set (+5.2% 3m, +36.8% 12m), and the intelligence shows concrete capital deployment riding that cycle: Zambia's ~$10bn four-year mining capex plan and the $710M Luanshya redevelopment targeting >1Mt copper output in 2026, DRC's Kamoa-Kakula-anchored Ivanhoe project, and Angola's Lobito Corridor logistics buildout explicitly enabling copper/rare-earth export growth (AfDB, July 2026). The Mozambique/Kenya conflict-leads-copper correlation (r=0.65-0.70) further flags that copper-linked resource-corridor activity is generating measurable on-the-ground economic signal, consistent with a live investment cycle rather than a dormant one.
supporting_signals: Copper +5.2% 3m / +36.8% 12m (Yahoo Finance, 2026-07)
Zambia: ~$10bn mining capex over 4 years (Mines Minister Kabuswe) plus $710M Luanshya redevelopment targeting August 2026 output
Angola: Lobito Corridor $553M DFC lending + $800M World Bank PPI port/rail rehab, linked to ~$2bn nondiamond mining/rare earth investment (AfDB, July 2026)
DRC: Ivanhoe Kamoa-Kakula copper complex and Port of Banana $1.2B seaport concession signal sustained capital absorption in copper logistics
risks: Copper price momentum could reverse sharply if China demand or global risk sentiment turns (as the South Sudan correlation note warns, metals correlations may reflect a common global cycle rather than durable fundamentals)
DRC/Zambia security and expropriation risk remains structurally elevated; FQVLF and IVPAF are thinly traded with material single-country concentration
Currency and repatriation risk in kwacha/Congolese franc could erode USD returns even if copper prices hold
Lobito Corridor and Luanshya projects are multi-year builds -- execution slippage could delay the offtake/production ramp this thesis assumes

theses.headline: Gold-mining equities with West African production bases stay bid over 6-12 months as gold's 12-month rally (+26.4%) persists alongside state-partnership extractives momentum in Mali, Burkina Faso and Sudan.
theses.geography: Mali / Burkina Faso / Sudan / West Africa
theses.rationale: Gold remains up 26.4% over 12 months even after a 9.5% three-month pullback, and West African/Sahel gold production is structurally central to state finances: Barrick's Loulo-Gounkoto complex in Mali survived a provisional-administration dispute and reverted to Barrick control (a template for recontracting risk resolution), Burkina Faso is raising state stakes in gold (Kiaka mine to 40%, Sovereign Mining Investment Fund announced May 2026) given gold is >80% of exports, and Sudan's gold sector is exceeding production targets (113% of Q1 2026 collection target) despite ongoing conflict, channeled to the UAE market. This is a case where extractive capital keeps flowing even through political rupture, supporting continued mine-level cash generation for exposed operators.
supporting_signals: Gold +26.4% over 12 months (Yahoo Finance, 2026-07)
Mali: Barrick's Loulo-Gounkoto complex regained operator control after provisional administration -- demonstrates recontracting-risk recovery template
Burkina Faso: Sovereign Mining Investment Fund (Siniyan-Sigui, May 21 2026) and state stake increase in Kiaka gold mine to 40% (April 21 2026), with gold >80% of export revenue
Sudan: gold-sector collection at 113% of Q1 2026 target and 89% of production plan (Sudan Tribune, April 23 2026) despite active conflict
risks: Gold's 3-month momentum has already turned negative (-9.5%), and a continued pullback would undercut the price-support leg of the thesis
Sahel state-partnership models (rising government equity stakes) raise expropriation/renegotiation risk that could compress producer margins even as production continues
Sudan gold exposure is not directly investable given conflict and sanctions context -- thesis relies on regional West African producers rather than Sudan itself
GDX and GOLD carry concentrated single-region operational risk (security incidents, fuel/logistics disruption in the Sahel) beyond normal mining-equity volatility

theses.headline: Guinea-linked diversified miners and Simandou-adjacent infrastructure plays benefit over 18 months as iron-ore-linked power and logistics buildout accelerates ahead of Simandou 2040.
theses.rationale: Guinea's government is explicitly sequencing power infrastructure to Simandou's ramp: PM Amadou Oury Bah's June 28, 2026 call for power-sector transformation to support 'Simandou 2040' is backed by concrete bankable precedent -- the 180MW Kankan-Siguiri-Kouroussa-Boké-Linsan solar PV project and the earlier $76.5M Boké solar park (World Bank PPI). Rio Tinto's direct Simandou iron-ore exposure makes it the natural large-cap vehicle, though iron ore itself is the weakest-momentum metal in the basket (-8.3% 3m, -0.9% 12m), meaning this is an infrastructure-buildout and market-share story more than a price-momentum one.

theses.headline: Cocoa-exposed agribusiness processors and soft-commodity futures stay elevated over 6 months as West African (Ghana/Ivory Coast) cocoa supply tightness drives a 61% three-month price spike.
theses.rationale: Cocoa is up 61.0% over three months -- by far the sharpest commodity move in the entire dataset -- even as it remains down 38.4% over 12 months, indicating a violent recent supply-side repricing centered on the two dominant West African producers. Ghana's COCOBOD syndicated financing facility (Bank of China/ICBC, ~$53-54M annual tranches within a $1.3-1.5bn structure) demonstrates that receivables-backed financing around cocoa persists across seasons, while Ivory Coast's National Development Plan explicitly targets agriculture as one of three pillars for its $209bn 2030 investment push (70% private capital). Global trading houses and processors (ADM, BG) that originate and process West African cocoa are the natural equity expression, since no direct Ghana/Ivory Coast cocoa equity exists on the instrument list.
supporting_signals: Cocoa +61.0% over 3 months (vs. -38.4% over 12 months) -- the sharpest short-term repricing in the commodity set (Yahoo Finance, 2026-07)
Ghana: recurring multi-year, multi-bank COCOBOD syndicated facility (~$1.3-1.5bn, 2020-2021 tranches) signals structured, repeatable cocoa-receivables financing
Ivory Coast: National Development Plan targets $209bn investment through 2030 with agriculture as an explicit pillar and 70% private-capital intent (allAfrica, July 7 2026)
Ivory Coast's Strategic Sovereign Development Fund (April 2026), financed by mining/energy revenue, signals state co-financing capacity that could extend to agriculture value-chain infrastructure
risks: A 61% three-month spike is a classic reversal-risk setup -- cocoa remains down 38.4% over 12 months, meaning the rally could be a short squeeze rather than a durable repricing
ADM and BG are globally diversified agribusiness majors with cocoa as one input among many -- heavy dilution versus a pure West African cocoa play
Ghana and Ivory Coast cocoa-sector finances are exposed to farmgate-price regulation and government marketing-board policy shifts that can decouple local producer economics from world price moves
No direct cocoa-futures-linked equity or regional ETF exists on the approved list, forcing reliance on either diversified processors or the futures contract itself

moderate.name: Archer-Daniels-Midland

theses.headline: Kenyan fintech, capital-markets and renewable-power exposure firms over the next 3-6 months as Kenya's unrest-to-investment lead indicator points to a fresh wave of deal activity.
theses.rationale: The firm's own correlation work shows Kenyan conflict/protest/political-violence events leading investment_events by roughly three months (r≈0.58, n=62, the most data-rich series in the set), consistent with an electoral/policy calendar that produces both unrest and a subsequent investment wave. This dovetails with concrete, already-visible momentum: Nairobi's NIFC push (15 newly certified firms, targeted $200M in fresh capital across digital finance/AI/carbon markets) and NSE market cap at an all-time high (KSh3.73 trillion H1 2026), alongside ATIDI's $960M mobilization for Lake Turkana Wind, Kipeto Wind and Menengai Geothermal and DFC's continued fintech lending (M-Kopa $51M, Mogo Auto $10M). The unrest-leads-investment pattern argues for treating any near-term Kenyan political-violence upticks as a potential entry signal rather than a pure risk flag.

theses.rationale: South Africa presents the most creditworthy improving-fundamentals story in the dataset: back-to-back sovereign rating upgrades from Moody's (May 2026), S&P (June 1 2026) and Fitch (June 5 2026), tied to a third consecutive primary fiscal surplus, lower the cost of capital for co-financed infrastructure. theses.headline: Mozambique-linked LNG value chain and regional gas/oil majors benefit over 18-24 months as TotalEnergies' Mozambique LNG restart and ExxonMobil's pending Rovuma FID unlock a multi-year hydrocarbons capex cycle.
theses.rationale: Mozambique's hydrocarbons cycle is the clearest multi-year, large-ticket capital commitment in the entire dataset: TotalEnergies' $20 billion LNG project (40% built, first gas targeted 2029) is restarting, and ExxonMobil's $30 billion Rovuma LNG project awaits an FID by September 2026, both requiring ancillary logistics, workforce housing, and services investment per President Chapo's June 2026 statements. This is reinforced by DFC/World Bank PPI commitments concentrated in power transmission tied to the LNG corridor ($450M Chimuara-Nacala transmission, $270M Namaacha wind farm), suggesting the broader grid and infrastructure ecosystem is being built out in parallel with the hydrocarbons capex wave.

DFC/World Bank PPI: $450M Chimuara-Nacala transmission project and $270M Namaacha wind farm (2024), signaling grid-expansion tied to the LNG corridor
